articleBlocks: At first glance, this puzzle felt like a collection of vacation destinations.
The clues evoked images of scenic views, hiking trails, and perhaps even skiing.
I started thinking about popular tourist spots around the world.
But that theory broke down as I considered the specific nature of each clue.
The 'Rockies' clue was the turning point.
It made me think of mountain ranges more specifically.
That's when I realized each clue referred to a major mountain range.
The answer is: Names of mountain ranges.
The Dolomites, Rockies, Andes, Alps, and Himalayas all fit perfectly.
The initial misdirection faded away, replaced by the clean fit of mountain ranges.
The puzzle highlights the importance of considering the specific nature of each clue to find the correct category.
solutionNarrative: Dolomites and Rockies first pulled me toward tourist attractions, so that was the first path I tested. It held together for a moment, but rockies never really fit it. The more I pushed that first read, the more the board sounded stitched together instead of naturally solved.

The solve turned when I stopped treating rockies as just another clue and asked what kind of thing each clue could really be describing. Once I made that shift, I was no longer thinking about tourist attractions; I was checking whether the earlier clues all behaved like parts of the same real set. That was when the answer became clear, because the remaining clues stopped feeling like separate trivia and started reinforcing the real category.
